history.dynasty: Built during the Kachhwaha period of Jaipur; local sources credit Vidyadhar Bhattacharya (Jaipur's chief architect) as the creator (believed - verify)
history.period: 18th century (one Jaipur guide dates the structure to 1784 AD; Wikipedia says the temple dates to Jaipur's founding circa 1727 CE or possibly earlier - conflict flagged)
history.summary: Identity confirmed: the old-city Shiva temple on Chaura Rasta (Choura Rasta) near Tripolia gate, Jaipur. The temple is named after the palm (tad) trees that once stood in the area. The Shivalinga is considered swayambhu (self-manifested); the installed lingam is black stone about 9 inches in diameter. Jaipur is called 'Chhoti Kashi' (Little Kashi) for its many ancient Shiva temples, of which this is a prominent one. Features a marble floor, a Jagmohan assembly hall, four bronze gongs of 125 kg each, a brass Nandi and golden pictographs. Coordinates from geocoding of the Chaura Rasta address agree with Wikipedia's 26.922964, 75.822593.

name: Tarkeshwar Nath Temple
town_description: Jaipur, the capital of Rajasthan, is the Pink City founded in 1727 by Sawai Jai Singh II - a planned walled city of bazaars, palaces and temples, and the gateway city for Rajasthan tourism.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport is ~12 km from the old city (verify).
travel.railway: Jaipur Junction is ~4-5 km from Chaura Rasta (verify).
travel.road: Chaura Rasta in the walled old city, off Johari Bazaar; reach by auto-rickshaw or taxi from Jaipur Junction or the city centre.

visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:30 AM to 10:45 PM daily per the temple's Google listing (verify locally; Wednesday hours appear unreliable in the listing). Morning abhisheka and Monday worship are the busiest periods.
